links.claim: A writer-signed refund after EscrowFinish is a different operation. Successful finish has already paid the writer and published the key. A subsequent quality challenge cannot reverse that transaction unilaterally. The writer may voluntarily sign a separate Payment returning money to the buyer. The receipt must distinguish that cooperative refund from expiry cancellation, even when both leave the buyer with returned principal.

links.claim: Retries must reuse the original obligation. The buyer journals the exact signed create blob before submission, and the writer journals its key and signed finish before submitting. Recovery can therefore inspect the original object or its terminal history rather than submitting another purchase. An absent object with no terminal transaction remains uncertain. The product guarantees one charge for each policy intent; it cannot prevent arbitrary wallet transactions performed outside the engine.

The interface shows paid, refunded and reserved amounts separately so that the user can understand both economic outcome and outstanding exposure.

sources.title: Writer no-show: EscrowCancel, key deadlines and writer-signed refunds
sources.body:
Writer no-show recovery starts with a durable purchase intent. The buyer has reserved budget and submitted an EscrowCreate, but the writer has not yet published a usable key. The principal is locked in an escrow object rather than transferred directly to the writer. The buyer must retain the signed quote, object identity and transaction hash while waiting. A missing HTTP response is not permission to buy the article a second time.

CancelAfter is a ledger deadline. Passing that deadline permits an EscrowCancel; it does not automatically move funds back to the buyer. Policy submits the cancellation and observes a successful validated transaction before recording principal returned. During network uncertainty the engine keeps the reservation pending. Local wall time and a countdown in the interface are useful indications, but the validated ledger determines whether cancellation is available.

EscrowCancel returns the original principal when the writer never completes delivery. The transaction fees remain spent. In our documented XRP example a cancelled sixty-thousand-drop principal returned in full, while create and cancel fees together consumed twenty-four drops. These figures describe a historical Testnet observation. They do not promise identical fees under future network load and do not express the principal as real SGD.

A writer-signed refund after EscrowFinish is a different operation. Successful finish has already paid the writer and published the key. A subsequent quality challenge cannot reverse that transaction unilaterally. The writer may voluntarily sign a separate Payment returning money to the buyer. The demonstration uses a cooperative seller. Outside that fixture, repayment depends on the seller's consent and cannot be compelled by this protocol. The receipt must distinguish that cooperative refund from expiry cancellation, even when both leave the buyer with returned principal.

The key-reveal mechanism makes publication of a key atomic with settlement, but it does not make prose true. The writer can sign a promise and deliver content that breaks it. The engine checks the authenticated envelope and salted passages privately, quarantines failed content, and records a failed claim. A fraud proof establishes which signed promise failed. Reputation and an explicit challenge handle that outcome; the ledger itself does not adjudicate the usefulness of an article.

Retries must reuse the original obligation. The buyer journals the exact signed create blob before submission, and the writer journals its key and signed finish before submitting. Recovery can therefore inspect the original object or its terminal history rather than submitting another purchase. An absent object with no terminal transaction remains uncertain. The product guarantees one charge for each policy intent; it cannot prevent arbitrary wallet transactions performed outside the engine.

Replacement expertise is a new intent with a separately reserved budget amount. A refund does not replenish gross spending authorization. Otherwise a series of bad purchases and refunds could exceed the user limit while the display reported a harmless net spend. The interface shows paid, refunded and reserved amounts separately so that the user can understand both economic outcome and outstanding exposure.

This note adapts docs/key-reveal-escrow.md and docs/BUILDER-FEEDBACK.md. Public faucet balances have no real value, and no mainnet protection is claimed. Show principal returned only after verified cancellation, refunded only after the separate refund settles, and pending while evidence is unresolved. The exact same labels should appear in live activity, receipts and replay so that a finance reviewer can reconcile them without guessing.
